topic: PM addresses Rohingya crisis at UN
headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[joins UN meeting on Rohingya crisis]] in New York
headline: PM Tarique Rahman joins UN meeting on Rohingya crisis in New York
summary: Co-hosted by Bangladesh and Gambia, the high-level session aims to pressure Myanmar for safe and dignified repatriation of the displaced people.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has joined a high-level meeting on the Rohingya crisis at the UN Headquarters in New York on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.

The session, titled “The Rohingya Crisis: A Renewed Call for a Durable Solution from Protracted Displacement, with Justice and Accountability”, was co-hosted by Bangladesh and Gambia with European Union support.
Representatives from eight countries attended, including Turkiye and Kuwait, representing the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).
The Prime Minister is expected to deliver an important speech during the meeting to sustain international attention and address the root causes of the crisis, including human rights.
The primary goal of the meeting is to pressure Myanmar to take back the Rohingya people and ensure a lasting solution to the displacement.
On Tuesday, PM Tarique also discussed the crisis with UN High Commissioner for Refugees Barham Salih, emphasizing that safe and dignified repatriation is the only lasting solution.
He stressed that achieving this requires more effective and coordinated international efforts to resolve the protracted displacement.

The Prime Minister is expected to deliver an important speech during the meeting to sustain international attention and address the root causes of the crisis, including human rights.

The primary goal of the meeting is to pressure Myanmar to take back the Rohingya people and ensure a lasting solution to the displacement.

headline: Foodpanda Bangladesh top officials face arrest warrants over fraud allegations
summary: Five executives of the food delivery giant have been accused in two separate cases involving fraud and criminal breach of trust. The court has issued warrants for their arrest.
details: A Dhaka court has issued arrest warrants for five high-ranking officials of Foodpanda Bangladesh in connection with two cases alleging fraud and criminal breach of trust. The accused include the Co-founder and Managing Director Syeda Ambareen Reza, Co-founder and Director Zubair Siddiky, Pandamart Director Mohammad Tabrej Khan, Head of Category Delara Farooq, and Senior Manager Mohammad Sajadul Haque.

The cases were filed on July 3 last year by Shihab Mahmud Bashir, proprietor of IPEl Distribution Network. Gulshan police submitted their probe reports to the court in June and July this year, leading to the issuance of the arrest warrants.

Delivery Hero Stores (Bangladesh), a sister company of Foodpanda, has stated that they will contest the allegations. In a statement, they expressed their commitment to working with the courts to resolve the dispute, emphasizing that the issues are commercial or contractual in nature and do not involve criminal liability on the part of their employees.
